newsitem.title: UK: Ockham assets soar as deals allow push into motor insurance.
newsitem.headline: Ockham assets soar as deals allow push into motor insurance.

text.p: Ockham Holdings, the Lloyd's of London insurance group, saw its assets soar from 236,000 pounds ($387,300) to over 27 million pounds on Thursday after two major refinancing deals.

Ockham announced it had sold its entire aviation and non-marine underwriting business to Bermudian insurance group ACE for 19.5 million pounds, while retaining a right to profit commissions from business conducted in 1994 and 1995.
In addition it has invested 25 million pounds into its motor insurance operation which trades under the name Highway, meaning its underwriting capacity can go up to 125 million.
The package involves 21 million pounds from U.S. investors Questor, headed by the influential merchant banker Dan Lufkin, and four million pounds From Ockham Holdings.
The twin deals mean Ockham pulls out of global commercial risks insurance and focuses on the lucrative motor insurance market using its two remaining Lloyd's syndicates.
David Poole, chief executive of Ockham, told Reuters: "We have spent two years in planning and this is the final step in the turnaround."

"We have gone through the process of ringfencing past liabilities and looked at the future. It was clear that with the huge companies now operating in the international market we would find it very difficult to compete," said Poole.
"When ACE came along and made an offer it was clearly at a level we should accept," he said. ($1=.6093 Pound)
